episode_title: Why Your Dental Membership Plan Stopped Growing

real_qa.q: What percentage discount should a dental membership plan offer to encourage enrollment without harming practice profitability?
real_qa.r: Research through A-B split testing in 1,200 practices tested discounts of 20%, 18%, 15%, 12%, 10%, and 8%. The answer that came back overwhelmingly was 10%—enough to encourage someone to sign up but with much lesser impact on the practice compared to the 45% average discount provided by PPO plans.

real_qa.q: What services should be included in an in-office dental membership plan design?
real_qa.r: The ideal plan should include two regular cleanings per year with accompanying exams and x-rays. Some offices add value-added services like fluoride, sealants, or annual take-home whitening. The plan typically also provides a percentage discount on any other service in the practice. The key advantage is locking patients into the practice on a regular recurring basis for routine care.
real_qa.requete: dental membership plan covered services benefits

real_qa.q: What percentage of adult Americans lack dental insurance coverage?
real_qa.r: More than half of adult Americans are not part of a PPO plan and still need dentistry. These uninsured patients represent a growing universe that includes retirees, gig economy workers like Uber and Lyft drivers, independent contractors, younger workforce members who haven't reached positions providing benefits, and those who are semi-retired.
real_qa.requete: percentage adult Americans without dental insurance

real_qa.q: How long have in-office dental membership plans existed as a practice strategy?
real_qa.r: Dental membership in-office membership plans have been around for 25 to 30 years, so they are not necessarily a new thing. However, most offices have them but they are poorly utilized, sitting on a shelf gathering dust despite their significant potential to grow a practice.
real_qa.requete: history dental membership plans years existed

real_qa.q: What is the average PPO discount that dental practices must accept from insurance plans?
real_qa.r: The average discount in a PPO plan today is 45%, meaning practices write off 45% of their standard fees when patients use PPO coverage. This makes in-office membership plans with smaller discounts (such as 10%) significantly more favorable for dental practice profitability.
